archetype.name: Surprise Contender (lineup-first)
archetype.definition: A club coming off 102 losses that hit its way to a winning record, a near-miss for the division and a Wild Card series win, while its pitching stayed league-average at best.

report.headline: A lineup-built leap from 102 losses to one ALDS win short

recap.finish: 84-78, second in the AL Central by one game; swept HOU 2-0 in the Wild Card Series, lost the ALDS 2-3 to CLE
recap.body:
Two years removed from 41-121 and one from 60-102, the White Sox won 84 games, a 24-win jump, and looked like a real winning team rather than a fluke. Their run differential of +0.35 per game (9th) works out to about +56 runs over the season, and the W vs Run Diff of -2.5 says the record undersold them. The identity was lopsided: the offense ranked 5th in runs per game and the hitters graded B+, while run prevention sat 15th, the rotation graded D and the bullpen C+.

The season was made in May. After a 1-4 opening week in which they were outscored 42-21 and a 13-13 April, they went 18-10 in May and outscored opponents by 32. Every month after that landed within a game of .500: 13-12, 13-12, 14-14, 12-13. They never won more than five straight or lost more than four. The flat record hid some swings underneath. July was the best run-prevention month (95 allowed), August the worst (140), and in September they outscored opponents by 15 and still finished 12-13. They closed 7-3, but lost the division to Cleveland by a single game, about the margin the close-game shortfall cost them.

Miguel Vargas drove the lineup: 5.3 WAR, a 134 wRC+, 33 homers and 22 steals, and the top third baseman on the site's tab. Chase Meidroth (4.5 WAR, 118 wRC+), Tristan Peters (3.5 WAR) and Sam Antonacci (.370 OBP) kept the line moving. Munetaka Murakami's 35 homers produced a 129 wRC+ despite a .207 average. Colson Montgomery hit 31 homers and saved 9.9 runs at short, but his .282 OBP kept him below average at the plate. The quieter story is the glove: +9.1 Fielding Runs, after five straight negative seasons that bottomed out at -33.3 in 2024. On the mound, Sean Burke (3.34 ERA, 185 strikeouts) and Davis Martin (3.95) were the only reliable starters. Luis Castillo's 5.85 ERA over 130.2 innings and Noah Schultz's 5.57 dragged the group down. Grant Taylor (2.25 ERA, 31.5% K) anchored a bullpen that was good at the top and thin beneath.

October started perfectly. They won 6-3 and 7-3 in Houston, then took the first two ALDS games in Cleveland, 3-0 and 4-3. Back home, the pitching gave way in 9-3 and 9-5 losses, and the bats went quiet in a 2-0 Game 5 loss. Over the ALDS they were outscored 23-15. The postseason OPS of .611 tells the story: Murakami managed a 54 wRC+, Braden Montgomery -9 and catcher Kyle Teel 41. Burke was superb (14.1 innings, 34.6% K, 0.70 WHIP). The rest of the listed starters combined for 9 innings, so the series was pitched by Burke and the bullpen.

The season leaves a lineup and defense that look like a contender's core and a rotation that does not. The run differential was earned, the record was if anything unlucky, and the gap between this team and a division title is mostly two or three starting pitchers.

highlights.title: Vargas leads a top-five offense
highlights.body: The offense ranked 5th in runs per game behind a B+ hitter group. Five regulars posted a wRC+ of 118 or better, so the production was broad-based. Vargas was the engine, combining on-base skill, power and speed in an All-Star season. It looks durable because it doesn't lean on one hot bat.

highlights.title: Defense flips from liability to asset
highlights.body: After years of bleeding runs in the field, the White Sox finished +9.1 in Fielding Runs, a swing of more than 31 runs from 2025. Colson Montgomery at short, Peters in the outfield and Meidroth at second all graded clearly positive. That swing is a large part of how a middling staff still allowed only league-average runs.

highlights.title: Taylor and Newcomb hold the late innings
highlights.body: Grant Taylor struck out 31.5% of batters with a 2.25 ERA, and a 2.77 FIP backs it up. Sean Newcomb added 90.1 innings at a 3.09 ERA. Both carried their form into October, which is why the bullpen kept the postseason close even when the starters couldn't go deep.

lowlights.title: A rotation that ends with Burke
lowlights.body: The rotation graded D. Beyond Burke and Martin, Castillo (5.85 ERA) and Schultz (5.57) gave up runs in bunches, and Kay's 4.44 ERA came with a 4.75 FIP that suggests he was fortunate to get there. The weakness showed again in October, when Burke was the only starter trusted with real innings.

lowlights.title: Division lost to close games
lowlights.body: A W vs Run Diff of -2.5 ranked 21st, and Cleveland won the Central by one game. September captured it: they outscored opponents by 15 and still went 12-13. Close-game outcomes mostly even out, so this reads as bad luck rather than a flaw.

lowlights.title: The bats vanished in the ALDS
lowlights.body: Up 2-0 on Cleveland, the White Sox scored 8 runs over the last three games and were shut out in the clincher. The postseason OPS of .611 was well below the regular-season .726, with Murakami and Braden Montgomery the coldest. Seven games is a small sample, but it ended a season that had earned more.

arc.note: After a 1-4 opening week and a .500 April, an 18-10 May built the cushion, and every month after landed within a game of .500. The longest streaks were five wins and four losses.

recap.nextYear: The lineup carries over as the strength. Vargas, Meidroth, Peters, Antonacci and Murakami all produced well above average, and the defense finally added runs instead of costing them. The holes in the order are specific: Benintendi was replacement-level at DH (-0.1 WAR, 98 wRC+), Acuña's 50 wRC+ in 224 PA was a drain, and Colson Montgomery's power comes with a .282 OBP. The rotation is the group that needs work most. Behind Burke and Martin it was a D-grade staff, and Erick Fedde's 3.83 ERA over 141 innings sits on a 5.01 FIP that points to regression. The luck ran against them: the run differential supported something like 86 or 87 wins, so the underlying team was a bit better than 84-78, and a mid-rotation upgrade would turn a one-game miss into a division-level club.

confidence.note: Full 162-game season; postseason read rests on just seven games.
